title: Difference of truncated hitting times
statement: Let $G$ be a finite $D$-regular multigraph with $D>0$, and let $b,c,x$ be vertices. For each target $t$ and starting vertex $v$, define $H_K(t,v)$ as the sum, over $0\le j<K$, of the probabilities that a uniformly chosen indexed-neighbor walk of length $j$ from $v$ avoids $t$ at every visited vertex, including its endpoint. Then for all integers $N,M\ge0$, $H_N(c,x)-H_N(c,b)\le H_M(b,x)+Nq_M(b,x)$, where $q_M(b,x)$ is the probability that such a length-$M$ walk from $x$ avoids $b$ at every visited vertex, including its endpoint.
hypotheses_covered: $G$ is a finite regular multigraph of degree $D$
